diagnosis:
Promotions and purchases die at three layers, and only the first is a weights problem.

1) LEAF EVAL (certain: arithmetic, three independent static measurements, and now ladder data). Cash is priced exactly like units: w[BankLiquid]=w[BankExcess]=100 (muju/src/ai/hard/eval/weights.ts:23-24; features at eval/features.ts:190-191) and material[] = cost x 100 (config.ts:506-513, scored at eval/evaluate.ts:122-131). So a promotion's material gain is cancelled by the bank loss, and then EconDelta at weight 100 (weights.ts:25; features.ts:506) charges the new rent through the forecast (tables/phasing-economy.ts:219: paidRent discounted 0.9^k over 6 closures = 4.22 crystals per upkeep crystal, truncated to 4). Net: every promotion is worth about -400 cc, NOT neutral as the lead assumed (median -400 over 860 sibling pairs; mean -391 over 847; <1% positive over 5,525 legal promotions). Nothing pays it back because all 57 combat/home/geometry features are 0. A purchase is exactly 0 in 9 of 12 probed positions, because the service PV is dropped whenever the commitment is flagged at risk (eval/pending.ts:116), and an exact tie goes to the first-ordered plain turn. The old 43b87b6 vector does not fix this: it charges rent twice (Rent -422 plus the rent leg inside EconDelta), promotions score -372 to -882.

2) BEAM CUT (high confidence). The within-turn scorer that fills the K=24 root list is stage0+stage1 only (engine.ts:355-360; used at gen/generate.ts:879, tie/evict rule at :915). PendingValue is stage 2, so every BUY reads as -100 cc per crystal there and is evicted first: the best-static BUY turn was in the K=24 list in 2 of 12 positions. Lowering the bank weights fixes this too, which is why they are the master switch.

3) GENERATOR CEILING (high confidence, weight-independent). The mission gate (gen/promote.ts:196-197 returns -1; :252-253 skips) proposes only ~9% of legal promotions (504 of 5,525; fire_1->2, 53% of all opportunities, 1 of 2,940); 4 of 12 positions have no PROMOTE turn at any K. Purchase plans are truncated in enumeration order before sorting (gen/purchase.ts:443-463, config.ts:543), so the menu is fire_1-only and capped near 12 crystals per turn (457 fire / 35 lightning / 0 plant-water-metal bought in 96 games). One ordinary promotion per Prepare (generate.ts:219-232).

LADDER CONFIRMATION (orchestrator's first-pass sweep, 32 games each vs Rush, wall:1500, rows flagged timing-void because the CPU is saturated, so treat as provisional): bootstrap 1/0/31, spend 27%, 0.1 promotions/game. Cash 90/25 alone: 12/0/20, spend 93%, 2.81 promotions/game, but 4 of 20 losses are now upkeep-elimination (it promotes into rent it cannot pay: RentShortfall/Inv7 are 0). Old priors: 7/0/25, 0.72 promotions. Home block alone: 4/0/28, spend 30%. m-combined (90/25 + old home + old tactical + sub-break-even tier premium): 7/0/25, 3.44 promotions. So: yes, a single knob (cash weight) switches spending and promoting on; it does not by itself make the engine win (16-23 losses per 32 are still plain elimination), and 7 vs 12 wins of 32 is only ~1.4 sigma, so nothing finer than 'broken vs working' is resolved yet.

Direct answer to the owner: four weight knobs each flip the sign of a promotion (BankExcess/BankLiquid down; tier-2/3 material[] up; TierClimb up; Rent POSITIVE ~+422..+525), all are safe to vary randomly or overshoot, and the variants below do exactly that. The ceiling on how much it can promote (roughly one proposed promotion per turn, never fire_1->2) is set by generator code, not weights.

WHAT TO VARY (8 numbers, all expressible as a weights JSON, so the existing MUJU_HARD_WEIGHTS hook is enough; extend /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ethancd-src-deevgames/d0196f82-8636-4254-b748-56de209f4b8e/scratchpad/weights/make-variants.ts with a seeded sampler):
 1. BankExcess: integer uniform in [0, 60] (switch is between 75 and 25; 25 is ladder-tested).
 2. BankLiquid: [60, 100].
 3. Tier premium m on tiers 2-3: log-uniform [1.3, 2.5] (break-even ~1.6 at cash 100, lower once cash is discounted); tier 1 fixed at cost x 100. Second round only: per-element premiums around the moderate table, +/-150 cc steps, enforcing T1 < T2 < T3.
 4. TierClimb: 0 with probability 0.5, else uniform [100, 800] (collinear with m, so read them jointly).
 5. Home-block scale h, 6. tactical-block scale t, 7. geometry/structure-block scale g: each 0 with probability 0.2, else log-uniform [0.4, 2.5], multiplying the v1 values of that block.
 8. RentShortfall: uniform [-600, 0]; Inv7PromoteNoRunway fixed at -600.
 Keep FIXED: PendingValue 1, w[Material] 100, EconDelta 100, tier-1 material, and 0 on the dead/broken/double-charging features (Rent negative, BankConvertible, ElementCoverage, DepletionWaste, RunwayCliff, Insolvency, RelocationDebt, Infiltration, CornerSeal, Inv1-6, Inv12, Inv14, Inv19, Inv20, ArrivalThreat, DisruptPressure). Rent positive [0, 600] may replace m in a separate round (it is collinear with m; never sample both).
 Config knobs that can be crossed in today with no code: K in {24, 48, 96} via hard@ablate:k48 / k96. purchase.maxPlans {12, 36, 105} x keepPerMultiset {3, 1} need the MUJU_HARD_PATCH hook first.

LOOP (successive halving, common random numbers):
 Stage A, screen: 24 samples + control + incumbent (currently 90/25). Each plays Rush, 8 pairs = 16 games, `--work wall:1500 --openings lab/hard-ai/ladder/openings/p1-dev.jsonl --pairs 8 --seed <S_A> --handicaps 0 --replays on`, the SAME seed and therefore the same opening rows and seat mirroring for every sample. Rush moves instantly, games are ~35-60 turns, so this is the cheapest decisive opponent (baseline 3% score). Read behaviour first, results second, from games.jsonl (players.<seat>.resourcesSpent / resourcesGained, promotions, unitsPlaced, winType, completedTurns; the orchestrator's sweep/stats.mjs already prints them): discard anything with spend < 50%, or upkeep-elimination in > 15% of games, or any illegal action / replica divergence. Keep the top 8 by score.
 Stage B: the 8 survivors play aiv2-hard-turn (the real target), 16 pairs = 32 games on p1-dev with a different seed S_B, plus 8 pairs vs Rush on S_B. Keep the top 3 by the SUM of the two scores (a candidate must improve against both: Rush punishes elimination, AIEngineV2 punishes the home corner). Regression guard: 8 pairs each vs Balanced and Expand (now 31/0/1 and 22/10/0); a candidate that drops there is a Rush counter-strategy (e.g. a turtle), not a better engine.
 Stage C, selection on held-out data: top 3 + control + incumbent on lab/hard-ai/ladder/openings/p1-val.jsonl, all 32 openings x 2 seats = 64 games vs aiv2-hard-turn and 32 vs Rush, fresh seed S_C never used before. Pick the winner ONLY from this table and report only these numbers; the dev numbers of a best-of-24 are inflated by roughly 2 standard errors (winner's curse). Optionally let the ladder decide with `--sprt -250,-100,0.05,0.05` vs aiv2-hard-turn (bootstrap is about -330 Elo: 11/3/82).

SPSA-STYLE REFINEMENT (only after random search has found the region): theta = the 8 numbers above, scaled so one unit is: cash 10 cc, m 0.15, block scales 25%, TierClimb 100, RentShortfall 75. Each iteration draws a +/-1 vector D, builds theta+cD and theta-cD, plays BOTH against Rush on the same 8 dev pairs and seed (16 games each), and moves theta by a_k x (score+ - score-) / (c x D), with a_k and c decaying (start a = 1 unit per 0.25 score difference, c = 1 unit); 30-50 iterations. Every 10 iterations gate theta on 16 pairs vs aiv2-hard-turn (dev) and revert if it dropped. A true head-to-head SPSA (theta+ vs theta-, `--work fixed:50000`, deterministic and immune to CPU load; fixed work is confined to hard@-vs-hard@ pairings, lab/hard-ai/ladder/engines.ts:36-40) needs the label-scoped hook first, and even then self-play shares both sides' blind spots (mission gate, fire-only buys), so use it for local polish only and never as the acceptance test.

HOW NOT TO FOOL OURSELVES:
 - Sample size honesty: per-game SD ~0.45, so n=16 has SE ~0.12, n=32 ~0.085, n=64 ~0.06. The effects found so far are huge (3% -> 38% vs Rush), so 16 games separate 'broken' from 'working', but they cannot rank working vectors: m-combined 7/32 vs m-bank-discount 12/32 is ~1.4 sigma. Treat any difference under ~20 points at n=32 as noise.
 - Hard is deterministic, so openings are the only real variance: 48 dev openings x 2 seats = at most 96 independent games per opponent. Re-running the same opening is not a new sample (wall-clock jitter only).
 - Dev is for tuning, val is for selection, sealed is never read (openings/ALLOCATION-P1.md). Count the looks at val (max 2-3 generations); anything chosen BECAUSE of a val result is no longer validated by it.
 - Always --pairs (seat mirroring), same seed within a stage (paired comparison), a new seed for confirmation (so nothing is fitted to one seed's opening draw).
 - Timing validity: the first-pass sweep rows are flagged 'harness VOID: timing' because 8 shards run on a saturated CPU under wall-clock budgets. Use those only as screens; re-run finalists (stage C) with the machine otherwise idle, or with fewer shards than cores.
 - Behaviour metrics are leading indicators, not goals: the two overshoot variants should show promotions and spend UP and wins DOWN; that bend is the point. Pre-register the primary metric (val score vs aiv2-hard-turn at wall:1500) and the guards (0 illegal actions, 0 replica divergences, upkeep-elimination rate, draw rate) before looking.
 - Keep DEFAULT_WEIGHTS frozen (M6-BOOTSTRAP-CONTRACT.md:96-106 pins weights 2/3 at 100 and material at cost); every candidate lives as a JSON file whose hash is stored next to its run directory, because the ladder manifest records only the config hash and label.

READING THE CURVES FROM THE FIXED SET: cash axis 100/100 (control) -> 85/40 (bank-discount) -> 90/25 (m-bank-discount, done) -> 50/0 (overshoot-bank-dump = m-bank-overshoot). Tier axis x1.0 -> x1.2/1.4 (m-tier-premium, below break-even) -> x1.6/2.2 (m-tier-overshoot, break-even) -> x1.75 (tier-premium) -> x3 (overshoot-material-x3).
